findings.problem: Every surface in this product is a countdown to one screen, and that screen has nothing on it. Driven at 1440 and at 390 it reads, in full: MARA & FINN / Today / Saturday 3 October 2026 / a rule / 'This is the day the plan was for.' / HAPPENING NOW: Wedding day / HOW YOU GOT HERE, 9 MOMENTS. That is the entire surface. The instrument that made 79 days legible - the rail, the ticks, the drawn distance - vanishes on the one morning the link is opened by everyone at once. It is also the only surface in the language that centres its text, so it composes as a memorial card rather than as this product: black ground, centred display word, a hairline, one quiet sentence. A family member opening it at eight in the morning learns nothing they did not already know, and the emotional arc of the whole product ends on a blank.
findings.fix: Give the morning the same instrument at the day's scale. Keep the horizon block (Today, the date, what the day is) left-aligned on the same edge every other surface uses and drop the centring. Below it run the measure over the moments dated 3 October, in order, on the same rail with the same ticks and the same mono date line, headed TODAY the way the approach is headed DAYS AWAY; where the record holds only one moment for the day, draw that one moment on the rail rather than collapsing it into a HAPPENING NOW label. Keep 'days back' folded underneath exactly as it is now. The morning should read as the same instrument measuring a shorter distance, not as a different product.

findings.element: state=phone and state=print, the received artifact
findings.problem: The engagement's own before-document names the defect by name: 'Nothing about it says wedding; swap the strings and it is a product roadmap.' The after is far more beautiful and the sentence is still true. What a guest receives is a calibrated measuring device listing the couple's admin - Send the invitations, Final dress fitting, Choose the evening music, Final guest numbers - with the edit buttons removed. There is exactly one warm human sentence anywhere in the artifact, 'Here is everything, love. It updates itself.', and it lives on the unfurl, above the card, inside the messaging app - so it is the one thing the guest reads and then never sees again the moment they tap through. The single surface the whole company will be judged on is the one with no person in it.
findings.fix: Carry the sender's line onto the surface it precedes. Store the one sentence typed at publish (the composition already exists on the unfurl) as the plan's dedication, and render it on the guest surface and on the keepsake, set in the reading face at title size and weight 400, on its own line directly under the project name and above the count, with no label and no quotation marks. Nothing else changes. It costs one field and one line of composition, and it is the difference between being handed an instrument and being handed a letter.

findings.element: state=print, driven at a real A4 viewport (794x1123) and printed to PDF
findings.problem: Judged as the physical object it claims to be, the keepsake fails. The sheet declares min-height 1123px and then renders 1935px of content: printed to A4 it comes out as two pages. Page one ends with the rail running off the bottom edge carrying nothing after 'Final guest numbers'; page two opens on a naked rail stub, places 'Wedding day' - the entire point of the object - a third of the way down, and leaves its bottom forty per cent blank. There is no break rule anywhere in the master. The two-column composition that every frame in the shots folder was captured at also does not survive: at true A4 width the container query drops to a single column, so the sheet that was reviewed is not the sheet that prints. And the only route back from paper, 'The plan stays online at https://timeline.signalstudio.ie/s/j7Qm2vK4xR9bT1nL6yH3cW8pZ5sD0aG7fJ4uE2rN9tM', is a forty-three character case-sensitive token that wraps mid-string across two lines. Nobody standing in a kitchen types that.
findings.fix: Make one page a constraint of the print state rather than a hint. Derive the print scale from the span instead of fixing it at ten pixels a day, so the last tick always lands above the footer whatever the horizon is. Set the print two-column grid by width rather than by container query, so the composition at A4 is the composition that was signed off. Add break-inside: avoid to every row and to the behind-you block so no row can ever be cut through. Where a plan genuinely will not fit, break deliberately after the last whole row and repeat the horizon block as a running head on sheet two rather than letting the rail spill. Replace the raw token in the footer with a short human code plus a QR block drawn in ink - a QR is a bitmap of ink, not a hue, so the palette holds.

findings.element: the sticky horizon block, state=owner-flight at 1280 and 1440
findings.problem: At desk the left column pins and stays. Scrolled to the bottom of the measure, looking at 19 September and 3 October, the pinned block still reads 'TODAY IS 16 JULY / Nothing is planned until 1 August.' It is not false, but it stopped describing anything on screen roughly six hundred pixels ago, and it is the closing line of a column whose lower two thirds are permanently empty. Half the desk window is a poster that says the same five things whether the reader is looking at July or at October. The emptiness reads as air on the first screen and as an unfinished column by the third.
findings.fix: Let the pinned block carry the one fact that changes as the reader travels. Keep the count, the date and 'Wedding day' fixed. Once the measure has scrolled past the first item, replace the gap note inside the pinned copy with a single mono line naming where the reader now is - YOU ARE AT 65 DAYS, LATE SEPTEMBER - derived from the topmost tick in the viewport through the same accessor every other count already uses. No hue, and no motion beyond a 0.08s cross-fade of that line's text on the declared easing, zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. The gap note keeps its place in normal flow at the top of the column, where it is true.

findings.element: the token layer and the .b-* composition primitives
findings.problem: Asked directly, could Notes be built from this without copying Timeline: half of it, yes. The materials are genuinely extractable - one fore/back/accent triad, matched eight-stop ink and paper ladders, a nine-stop gap ladder, leading and tracking bound to role rather than to size, three durations on one easing. Those transfer as they stand. The composition does not. Every primitive is named .b- for direction B, which is a lab artefact and not a vocabulary; and the one idea that gives this artifact its signature - position on the page is the quantity, drawn to scale - has no analogue in Notes or Tasks, neither of which has a scalar to measure. So a second product inherits a palette and a ruler and then invents its own organising object from scratch, which is exactly what the brief said must not happen. And nothing anywhere gives the language a name, so there is nothing for the next product to ask for.
findings.fix: Write the one page that names it and ship it beside lock.md. Give the language a name. List the transferable rules by their token names: the ink ladder and its eight stops, the gap ladder, leading-by-role, tracking-by-role, 0 / 0.08 / 0.14 / 0.22 on one easing, status by ink density and never by hue. List the honesty rules as language rather than as Timeline behaviour: every fact through one accessor, every condition stated in words as well as drawn, one reversibility surface in one place, state today wherever a date appears, anything not built has no button element. Then state the one composition rule that does generalise - the organising object is a quantity drawn to scale, and a product with no quantity gets no measure - and say plainly what Notes and Tasks must therefore choose for themselves. Rename the .b-* primitives to the language's own names before any second product reads them.

biggestWin: The empty rail. 'Nothing is planned until 1 August' is said once in a sentence and then drawn at full scale, so a fortnight of silence occupies a fortnight of the page, and the eye feels the wait before the mind reads it. That is one real idea, held without flinching across screen, phone and paper, and it is the only thing here a competitor could not copy without copying the whole instrument. The empty project runs it close: 'When is the day? Everything on this page is measured from it, so it is the only thing needed to start' is the best sentence in the product and the clearest first move I have seen on a first-run screen this year.
